task: For this synthetic writing exercise, use the fictional reporting notes to write a business and labor news story for a general newspaper audience. Write from this reporting snapshot as of April 16, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: Dockworkers at Port Calloway entered their third day of a work stoppage Wednesday, April 16, 2025, with an estimated $180 million in cargo sitting idle at the port.
The strike began Monday, April 14, 2025, when International Longshore Workers Union Local 14 rejected a management offer and walked off the job.
Local 14 president Maria Reyes said: "We move every container that keeps this economy running, and we have been offered less than inflation in real terms."
Port Calloway authority chief Donald Hsu said: "We remain committed to reaching a fair agreement, but this disruption is costing everyone."
The 890 striking dockworkers are seeking a 28 percent wage increase over four years; the port authority's current offer is 18 percent over the same period.

A second dispute centers on automation: the union wants the port to pause all new automation investment during contract negotiations; the port authority plans to install six new automated container cranes.
Approximately 2,100 containers are currently sitting at Port Calloway that would have been loaded or unloaded under normal operations.
Port Calloway handles approximately $4.2 billion in cargo annually and is a principal entry point for electronics, auto parts, and refrigerated agricultural products.

The Calloway Regional Chamber of Commerce estimated Wednesday the strike is costing the regional economy approximately $60 million per day in delayed commerce, including downstream supply chain disruptions.
The Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service dispatched a team to Calloway on Tuesday; team leader Gerald Watts said the parties had agreed to talk but had not yet entered formal mediated sessions.
The port's terminal operator redirected four arriving cargo ships to Port Westfield, 80 miles up the coast, adding an estimated $2,300 per container in handling and trucking costs.
The union's previous contract, which expired December 31, 2024, provided a 12 percent wage increase over a four-year term.
The port authority reported a $28 million operating surplus in fiscal year 2024.
The six automated cranes the port plans to purchase are estimated to reduce labor requirements by approximately 18 percent per shift once operational.
Reyes said automation was a "red line" for the union; Hsu said the cranes were necessary for the port to remain competitive with neighboring facilities.
The ILWU national leadership has not declared a formal national strike; Local 14 is acting independently under its own collective bargaining agreement.
The last major work stoppage at Port Calloway was in 2011 and lasted nine days; it was resolved with federal mediation.
Cargo perishables — including strawberry and lettuce shipments — accounted for roughly 12 percent of the stranded containers, according to port records.
The California Governor's office offered to assign a state mediator; the union said it was open, but port management said it preferred the federal process.
Three electronics importers and two auto parts distributors told reporters they had missed delivery deadlines; none agreed to be named publicly.
